text:
alice_customer: Hey team — running into duplicate POSTs to /v1/responses and duplicate billing events. We use the TS/Node SDK 1.3.2 in a Lambda-ish serverless container (Node 20). Only happens under load when tokens refresh.

maria_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste a minimal repro and any logs? Do you use idempotency keys?

alice_customer: No idempotency key on these requests. Minimal repro (simplified):
```ts
// creates client once per container, token is fetched via refresh flow
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });

async function call() {
  // simple request that has a JSON body
  await client.responses.create({ model: 'open-llama', input: 'hello' });
}

// under load we call call() concurrently, sometimes token fetch returns 401, refresh and we retry
```
Logs (sanitized):
```
2024-10-12T15:02:01Z Request start id=abc123
2024-10-12T15:02:01Z 401 token expired -> refresh start
2024-10-12T15:02:01Z Retry: reusing same request id=abc123
2024-10-12T15:02:01Z Request processed (server) id=abc123
```
This leads to server processing same body twice. Happens only on bursty traffic.

jack_eng: Two quick suspects: 1) body/stream was consumed and SDK/undici attempted to resend but the server actually got two requests (race between token refresh + retry). 2) AbortController or signal reuse across retries causing weird re-send semantics. Which undici/node-fetch stack are you on?

alice_customer: undici 5.12.0 (global fetch shim). Node 20. SDK 1.3.2 as I said.

leo_js-sdk: Thanks — that combination rings a bell. In SDK 1.3.2 we had a retry path that could reuse the same AbortSignal and request body when a token refresh race happened. undici's fetch will throw if body stream already used; but depending on how the retry was implemented we saw duplicated network calls in some edge cases.

maria_support: Can you try 2 quick workarounds so we can triage? 1) add an idempotency key header (x-idempotency-key) for the POSTs, 2) upgrade to SDK 1.3.6 (contains a retry fix) or at least to 1.3.4 which changed the retry/signal handling.

alice_customer: Ok I'll try. Any reproduction script you'd like me to run?

leo_js-sdk: If you can run this locally it should repro in a loop. It simulates concurrent requests and forces a token refresh by manually expiring the key between calls.
```bash
# repro.sh
node -e "const { RedwoodClient } = require('./src'); const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: 'TEMP' }); async function r(){ try{ await client.responses.create({ model:'x', input:'hi' }); }catch(e){ console.log('err', e.message); }}; for(i=0;i<200;i++){ r(); }"
```
Note: wrap with a token refresh stub that returns 401 for some calls. Also run with UNDICI_DEBUG=1 to capture low-level client logs.

jack_eng: Also check you are not reusing AbortController instances across retries. Each retry should create a fresh AbortController. If your app shares one per invocation container and the SDK was patched to reuse it, that might explain the weird ordering.

alice_customer: Ran with idempotency header and it already prevented duplicates on the server side in my local run. Will try upgrading SDK next and report back.

sre-bot: telemetry: incident-create? false, duplicate-requests-observed: true, suggested-labels: ["sdk:js","undici","retry"].

maria_support: Great. Action items: leo will add a small repro test in the SDK repo to validate non-reuse of AbortSignal across retries; jack will draft a short KB note recommending idempotency keys and SDK upgrade; alice will test SDK 1.3.6 and report. Thanks — ping here when you have results. :thumbsup:

leo_js-sdk: one more note for support engineers — if customer can't upgrade, we can backport a small patch to 1.3.2 that ensures body is cloned where possible and that retry creates a fresh signal. But cloning not always possible for streaming bodies, so idempotency is the safer fallback.

alice_customer: Thanks all, will update in a few hours after tests.
